importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation across prefabricated structures is extreme — a PEB industrial shed, portable cabin, modular office, and prefab toilet block are visually unrecognisable as the same category. Buyers use the image to identify product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Structure type, wall panel type, and material are non-interchangeable shortlisting criteria — a buyer needing a PUF-insulated cold storage warehouse cannot substitute a GI-sheet industrial shed. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated by buyers or sellers.

Per-sq-ft pricing varies substantially with structure type, panel specification, and span — buyers compare rates across sellers within their confirmed spec tier. Indian industrial and commercial buyers are price-aggressive; price is a primary decision lever once type and material match.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Per sq ft is dominant for PEB sheds and industrial warehouses (primary segment). Portable cabins and modular rooms are quoted per piece/unit; large turnkey institutional projects are quoted per project. Unit must be shown to prevent price comparison errors across sub-segments.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared without knowing the unit — per sq ft vs per piece vs per project creates genuine confusion across sub-segments. A buyer comparing a PEB shed listing (per sq ft) with a portable cabin listing (per unit) will misread price if unit is not shown.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: The Indian prefabricated structures market is fragmented across regional fabricators; buyers search by structure type and spec, not manufacturer name — EPACK, Interarch, and Metal Tree are known to repeat buyers but not searched by name by first-time buyers.
importance_ranking.reason: For capital projects, buyers evaluate manufacturer status, installation capability, IS code compliance track record, and erection experience during vendor selection — but these are post-shortlisting checks, not initial engagement drivers.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines what the product IS — industrial shed, warehouse, office, hospital, labour camp, toilet block are non-interchangeable; entire structural design, span, and per-sq-ft pricing changes with structure type.

Defines insulation grade and cladding quality — PUF panel (cold storage grade) vs GI sheet (basic industrial) represents a significant per-sq-ft price delta and is non-interchangeable for regulated applications such as cold storage and fire-rated buildings.

missing_important_specs.why_important: PEB and industrial shed buyers specify clear span (15m / 20m / 30m / 40m+) as the primary structural requirement — it determines column-free floor area and drives fabrication cost; sellers cannot confirm fit or price without it.

Institutional, government, and infrastructure buyers require IS 800 / IS 875 / IS 1893 compliance documentation as a procurement eligibility criterion — sellers without certified compliance are disqualified from these tenders.

Roofing material (PPGI colour-coated / GI plain / polycarbonate / insulated sandwich) affects weatherproofing performance and per-sq-ft cost independently of roof shape — buyers in high-rainfall or cold storage applications specify this separately from Roof Type.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Routes the RFQ to sellers who specialise in the right structure type — a cold storage PEB supplier cannot supply a labour camp, and application value immediately determines structural design, panel type, and compliance requirements.
Defines project scale — sellers need this to confirm minimum project eligibility, estimate structural span requirements, and provide a meaningful per-sq-ft price indication.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the buyer requires PUF (cold storage), EPS (standard industrial), rockwool (fire-rated), or GI sheet (basic shed) to determine product fit and price — this is a non-interchangeable requirement that cannot be resolved post-connection.
